'''''Numberphile''''' is an [[Educational entertainment|educational]] [[YouTube channel]] featuring videos that explore topics from a variety of [[fields of mathematics]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Schultz |first1=Colin |title=The Great Debate Over Whether 1+2+3+4..+ ∞ = −1/12 |url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/great-debate-over-whether-1234-112-180949559/ |website=Smithsonian Magazine }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Ryan |first1=Jackson |title=Earth is getting a black box to record events that lead to the downfall of civilization |url=https://www.cnet.com/news/earth-is-getting-a-black-box-to-record-events-that-lead-to-the-downfall-of-civilization/ |website=CNET |access-date=8 December 2021 |language=en}}</ref> In the early days of the channel, each video focused on a specific number, but the channel has since expanded its scope,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Merow |first=Sophia D. |date=2024-01-02 |title=A Duodecade of Numberphile: The "Original Maths YouTube Channel" Turns 12 |journal=Math Horizons |language=en |volume=31 |issue=1 |pages=20–23 |doi=10.1080/10724117.2023.2224682 |issn=1072-4117|doi-access=free }}</ref> featuring videos on more advanced mathematical concepts such as [[Fermat's Last Theorem]], the [[Riemann hypothesis]]<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lamb |first1=Evelyn |title=Does 1+2+3... Really Equal −1/12? |url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/roots-of-unity/does-123-really-equal-112/ |website=Scientific American Blog Network |access-date=8 December 2021}}</ref> and [[Kruskal's tree theorem]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bennett |first1=Jay |title=The Enormity of the Number TREE(3) Is Beyond Comprehension |url=https://www.popularmechanics.com/science/math/a28725/number-tree3/ |website=Popular Mechanics |access-date=8 December 2021 |date=20 October 2017}}</ref> The videos are produced by [[Brady Haran]], a former [[BBC]] video journalist and creator of [[Periodic Videos]], Sixty Symbols, and several other YouTube channels.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/tv/la-ca-st-science-programming-essay-20160403-column.html|title=As VidCon gets underway, science presenters rule the Web|first=Robert|last=Lloyd|work=Los Angeles Times|date=April 1, 2016}}</ref> Videos on the channel feature several university professors, maths communicators and famous mathematicians.<ref name="NegativeTwelthNYT">{{cite news |last1=Overbye |first1=Dennis |title=In the End, It All Adds Up to – 1/12 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/02/04/science/in-the-end-it-all-adds-up-to.html |access-date=8 December 2021 |work=[[The New York Times]]|date=3 February 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202210/rnoti-p1789.pdf|title=The World of YouTube Math Communication|first=Scott|last=Hershberger|publisher=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society|Notices Of The American Mathematical Society]]|date=November 2022}}</ref>

In 2018, Haran released a [[spin-off (media)|spin-off]] audio [[podcast]] titled ''The Numberphile Podcast''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bradyharanblog.com/blog/the-numberphile-podcast|title=The Numberphile Podcast|website=Brady Haran|date=11 November 2018 |access-date=25 December 2018}}</ref>

==YouTube channel==
The ''Numberphile'' YouTube channel was started on 15 September 2011. Most videos consist of Haran interviewing an expert on a number, [[mathematical theorem]] or other mathematical concept.<ref>
{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/grrlscientist/2012/mar/05/1|title=145 and the melancoil: What do narcissistic numbers and happy numbers share with the wild events that transpire when mathematicians visit the pub?|author=GrrlScientist|work=The Guardian|date=5 March 2012}}</ref> The expert usually draws out their explanation on a large piece of [[Kraft paper|brown paper]] and attempts to make the concepts understandable to the average, non-mathematician viewer.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/wonk/wp/2016/03/01/the-eerie-math-that-could-predict-terrorist-attacks/|title=ECONOMIC POLICY: The eerie math that could predict terrorist|first=Ana|last=Swanson|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=March 1, 2016}}</ref> It is supported by the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] (MSRI) and [[Math for America]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20181023165642/http://numberphile.com/MSRI/index.html Numberphile sponsors] Mathematical Sciences Research Institute</ref><ref name=shorty>[https://shortyawards.com/8th/numberphile Numberphile Nominated in Education] 8th Annual Shorty Awards</ref> Haran also runs the "Numberphile2" channel, which includes extra footage and further detail than the main channel.<ref name="About2">{{cite web |last1=Haran |first1=Brady |title=Numberphile2 |url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCyp1gCHZJU_fGWFf2rtMkCg/about |website=YouTube |access-date=17 October 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

===Reception===
Numberphile consistently rates among the top YouTube channels in math and education.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.educatorstechnology.com/2012/10/8-great-youtube-channels-for-math.html|title=Best YouTube Math Channels|first=Med|last=Kharbach|publisher=YouTube Channels for Teachers|date=December 18, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://history-computer.com/top-10-best-math-youtube-channels/|title=Top 10 Best Math YouTube Channels|first=Jacqueline|last=Michelle|work=History-Computer |publisher=History-Computer.com|date=December 21, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://youneedchannels.com/math-youtube-channels/|title=43 Best Math YouTube Channels Ranked by Popularity: #2 Numberphile|publisher=youneedchannels.com|date=November 20, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://abakcus.com/17-best-math-youtube-channels-to-study-mathematics/|title=17 Best Math Youtube Channels to Study Mathematics|publisher=Abakcus|date=January 24, 2023}}</ref> The channel was nominated for a [[Shorty Award]] in Education in 2016.<ref>{{cite journal|url= https://alexisjoyvipaccess.com/2016/01/19/article-the-8th-annual-shorty-awards-just-released-this-years-nominees-find-out-if-your-fav-was-nominated-here|title = The 8th Annual Shorty Award|journal=Alexis Joy|date=January 19, 2016}}</ref> ''[[The New York Times]]'' said that, "at Numberphile, mathematicians discourse, enthusiastically and winningly, on numbers", and ''[[The Independent]]'' described the channel as "insanely popular".<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/04/25/arts/television/youtubes-original-channels-take-on-tv.html|title=Genres Stretch, for Better and Worse, as YouTube Takes On TV|first1=Mike|last1=Hale|journal=The New York Times|date=April 24, 2012}}</ref><ref name="StandUpBeCounted">{{cite news |last1=Usborne |first1=Simon |title=Stand-up and Be Counted |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-independent-stand-up-and-be-counted/124357822/ |access-date=10 May 2023 |work=Newspapers.com |date=31 October 2014}}</ref> ''[[The Sunday Times]]'' said, "The mathematical stars of social media, such as James Grime and [[Matt Parker]], entertain legions of fans with striking videos demonstrating how powerful and playful maths can be."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/article/hannah-fry-teach-children-to-fall-in-love-with-maths-they-can-count-on-it-for-life-k5b5kgh0l|title=Teach children to fall in love with maths and they can count on it for life|first=Hannah|last=Fry|publisher=The Sunday Times|date=December 8, 2019}}</ref>

''[[New Scientist]]'' listed Numberphile as one of the top ten science channels on YouTube in 2019.<ref name="NewScientist2019">{{cite news |last1=Stokel-Walker |first1=Chris |title=YouTube science videos: The channels you should subscribe to |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg24132180-400-youtube-science-videos-the-channels-you-should-subscribe-to/ |access-date=10 May 2023 |work=New Scientist |date=20 February 2019}}</ref>

In 2024, Brady Haran was awarded the [[Christopher Zeeman#The Zeeman Medal|Christopher Zeeman Medal]] recognising excellence in the communication of mathematics for his work, including ''Numberphile''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brady Haran wins the 2024 Christopher Zeeman Medal |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news/brady-haran-2024-christopher-zeeman-medal |website=[[London Mathematical Society]] |publisher=London Mathematical Society |access-date=4 September 2024}}</ref>
